heroHeadline: Three-Front Peace Collapse: Ukraine Ceasefire Expires Without Extension; Lebanon 51 Killed in 24 Hours; Iran MOU Deadlocked as Trump Rejects Response
heroSubtitle: May 11, 2026 marks a day of compounded peace process failures across three active diplomatic tracks. The U.S.-brokered 72-hour Ukraine–Russia ceasefire (May 9–11) expired without extension on Day 3, with Russia claiming 16,071 Ukrainian violations and Ukraine documenting drone, bomb, and artillery attacks killing at least 2 civilians in Kharkiv and Kherson — no enforcement mechanism existed to adjudicate competing accusations. The only concrete deliverable — a 1,000-per-side prisoner of war exchange — is proceeding, but no diplomatic framework was established. President Putin conditioned any meeting with Zelensky on a full peace treaty being finalized first (not preliminary talks), and the EU flatly rejected Putin's nomination of former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder as Ukraine peace mediator (Kallas: 'not wise'). Simultaneously, U.S.–Iran MOU negotiations deadlocked after Trump reportedly rejected Iran's formal counterproposal — submitted May 10 via Pakistan's back-channel — as 'totally unacceptable,' with Iran reportedly having expanded demands beyond the narrow one-page MOU framework to include comprehensive sanctions relief, IRGC security guarantees, and an Iranian role managing Hormuz transit. Treasury yields moved higher on the breakdown. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed (~750 vessels trapped, U.S. gas $4.48/gal, highest since July 2022). On the third front, Lebanon's nominally active ceasefire collapsed in practice: 51 people were killed in Lebanon in a 24-hour period — the deadliest since the ceasefire was declared April 16 — after Israel bombed Beirut's southern suburbs (Ghobeiri) for the first time since the ceasefire began and Hezbollah launched 24 attacks using fiber-optic FPV drones, rockets, and missiles. Al Jazeera asked: 'Is even the pretence of a ceasefire over?' The May 14–15 Washington talks between Israel and Lebanon remain the last diplomatic lifeline on that front.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
